regression.comparison_scope: successful values/types or error stages; not full structured error-condition equivalence

delta.remaining_target_difference: The runner captures condition:null; its error text now has [ARITHMETIC_OVERFLOW] and the native overflow cause.

performance_protocol.comparison: checked ANSI versus wrapping arithmetic on non-overflowing input; different semantics
performance_protocol.memory: per-case output bytes and whole-process maximum RSS, not per-operator peak allocation
performance_protocol.statistic: median per process, then median across 4 processes; report all samples and paired ratios

remaining_cost: Batch 256 ordinary ANSI integer execution is 22.2%-62.5% slower than wrapping; nested NULL cases are 238.2%-263.2% slower.
The comparison changes semantics. Native checking, scalar dispatch, filtering/scattering and allocation costs are not separately attributed.
Controls vary, especially at batch 8192; there is no same-binary calibration or instruction-counter evidence in this run.
Output byte counts agree; whole-process RSS is not per-operator temporary peak allocation.
baseline_trait_note: Both builds share the unused default trait method. Only the candidate scalar evaluator and Spark UDF opt in; all 6,784 accepted baseline outcomes are preserved.

preservation.optional_selection: checked ANSI integer arithmetic is the correctness baseline for the next performance investigation
